explanation: Kourovka 19.25 asks: if |G| = |H|, Σφ(|g|) = Σφ(|h|), and G is simple, must H be simple? The Lean negates the universal claim, matching the "No" answer recorded in Kourovka v50, citing Monticone and van Doorn–Judin–Monticone–Morrison. I checked the counterexample by computation: PSU(3,3) (from its class sizes) and C6 × S4 × (C7⋊C6) both have order 6048 and totient sum 23984. The statement is correct and solved.
